name: Genetic Syndromic Esophageal Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of esophageal atresia or tracheoesophageal fistula confirmed by imaging or surgery
Presence of additional congenital anomalies consistent with known syndromic associations (e.g., VACTERL, CHARGE, Feingold syndrome)
Identification of pathogenic variant in genes known to cause syndromic esophageal malformations (e.g., SOX2, MYCN, CHD7)
Exclusion of isolated esophageal malformations without syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of esophageal atresia or tracheoesophageal fistula plus at least one additional syndromic feature or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including genetic testing and imaging studies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Esophageal atresia with or without tracheoesophageal fistula
Congenital feeding difficulties due to esophageal discontinuity
searchTerms: feeding problems due to esophagus gap

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent aspiration pneumonia secondary to fistula
searchTerms: repeated lung infections from food entering airway

common.symptomName: Congenital cardiac malformations (e.g., ventricular septal defect, tetralogy of Fallot)

occasional.symptomName: Ocular coloboma or other ophthalmological anomalies

occasional.notes: May be secondary to feeding difficulties

searchTerms: breathing problems not caused by choking

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing pathogenic variants in associated genes
Blood gas abnormalities due to aspiration
Possible electrolyte imbalances secondary to feeding difficulties
imaging: Contrast esophagram demonstrating esophageal discontinuity or fistula
Chest X-ray showing air in the stomach or lungs indicating fistula
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SOX2, MYCN, CHD7, or other genes linked to syndromic esophageal malformations
Chromosomal microarray or exome sequencing identifying syndromic causes
other: Multidisciplinary clinical assessment including feeding and respiratory evaluations

distinguishingFeatures: Negative genetic testing for syndromic causes
Isolated esophageal malformation without systemic involvement
Presence of vertebral, anal, cardiac, tracheoesophageal, renal, and limb anomalies
Diagnosis based on constellation of anomalies rather than isolated genetic cause
May overlap but requires broader systemic evaluation

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress due to aspiration
Failure to thrive despite feeding interventions
Multiple congenital anomalies suggesting syndromic involvement
references: Orphanet: Genetic Syndromic Esophageal Malformation - ORPHA:371445
Brosens E, et al. Syndromic esophageal atresia: clinical and genetic overview. Eur J Med Genet. 2021.
Lemoine S, et al. Genetic causes of esophageal malformations: a review. Clin Genet. 2023.
